slides.heading: Reception — Autumn 2, Week 1
slides.sub: New sounds taught directly, practised and applied in words, captions and the matching decodable book.

slides.heading: Mon
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "ck" (/k/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="duck" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="duck"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Kester the duckling snaps his beak shut quickly whenever he hears a click — 'ck, ck'.

character.name: Kester
character.blurb: Kester is a quick, alert duckling with a tuft of down on his head, always the first to snap his beak at a passing fly.

slides.pronunciation_note: Two letters, one sharp sound — 'ck' says exactly the same as 'k', usually at the end of short words.
slides.formation_cue: Write 'c', then 'k', close together — two letters, one sound.
slides.action: Clap your hands together once, sharply and quickly, like Kester's beak snapping shut, saying 'ck'.
slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="duck" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="duck"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.tip: In 'to' the o makes a long 'oo' sound instead of its short sound — think of it as a tiny pointing word, always heading off to somewhere.

slides.heading: Tue
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "e" (/ɛ/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="egg" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="egg"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Elsie the flower trembles her petals in the breeze — 'e, e, e'.

character.name: Elsie
character.blurb: Elsie is a bright, striped-petal flower who quivers gently whenever the smallest breeze passes by.

slides.pronunciation_note: A short, flat sound — 'e' as in 'egg', not the long letter name.
slides.formation_cue: Start on the left, halfway up the small letters. Go straight across to the right, then curve up, over and round to the left and along the bottom. Finish at the bottom right.
slides.formation_rhyme: Straight across, then curl all round.
slides.action: Give your fingers a tiny flutter near your chest, like Elsie's petals trembling, saying a short 'e'.
slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="egg" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="egg"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.heading: Wed
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "u" (/ʌ/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="umbrella" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="umbrella"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Una the butterfly dips down low, then lifts up, up, up into the air — 'u, u, u'.

character.name: Una
character.blurb: Una is a spotted butterfly who loves to dip down to a flower before lifting straight back up into the sky.

slides.pronunciation_note: A short, quick sound from the middle of the mouth — 'u' as in 'sun', not 'yoo'.
slides.formation_cue: Start at the top of the small letters. Pull down, curve round the bottom and up to the top, then straight back down. Finish on the line.
slides.formation_rhyme: Down, round the bottom, up and down.
slides.action: Scoop both hands from your waist up to your shoulders, like Una lifting off, saying a short 'u'.
slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="umbrella" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="umbrella"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.dictation: A cup is on a mat.

slides.heading: Thu
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "r" (/r/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="rug" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="rug"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Rusty the robin ruffles his feathers and growls out a proud 'rrr' from his branch.

character.name: Rusty
character.blurb: Rusty is a proud little robin with a bright red-berry chest who loves to ruffle his feathers before he sings.

slides.pronunciation_note: A growly sound you can hold, 'rrr', with the tongue pulled back and not touching the roof of the mouth — not rolled, and not 'ruh'.
slides.formation_cue: Start at the top of the small letters. Pull straight down, go back up the same line, then curve over to the right. Finish just past the top of the line.
slides.formation_rhyme: Down, back up, and flick over.
slides.action: Give your shoulders a quick shimmy, like Rusty ruffling his feathers, while making a soft growly 'rrr'.
slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="rug" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="rug"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.heading: Fri
slides.objective: Revisit everything taught this week, read the matched decodable book, and check how securely it has been learned.

slides.dictation: A dog sits on a rug.
